availableCommands.description: You MUST use this before any creative work - creating features, building components, adding functionality, or modifying behavior. Explores user intent, requirements and design before implementation.
availableCommands.name: $brainstorming

availableCommands.description: Create a new Harbor task for evaluating agents. Use when the user wants to scaffold, build, or design a new task, benchmark problem, or eval. Guides through instruction writing, environment setup, verifier design (pytest vs Reward Kit vs custom), and solution scripting.
availableCommands.name: $create-task

availableCommands.description: Helps users discover and install agent skills when they ask questions like "how do I do X", "find a skill for X", "is there a skill that can...", or express interest in extending capabilities. This skill should be used when the user is looking for functionality that might exist as an installable skill.
availableCommands.name: $find-skills

availableCommands.description: Kimi WebBridge lets AI control the user's real browser — navigate, click, type, read, screenshot, and interact with any website using the user's actual login sessions. Use this skill whenever the user wants to interact with websites, automate browser tasks, scrape web content, or perform any action requiring a real browser. Also use when the user mentions "browser", "webpage", "open URL", "screenshot", or asks to read/interact with any website. Use even for simple-sounding browser requests — the daemon handles all complexity.
availableCommands.name: $kimi-webbridge

availableCommands.description: Use when you're operating OpenRig and need the right skill or context for fleet recovery, seat handover, new-seat orientation, a watchdog wake, cross-host reach to an agent on another machine, rig packaging, an OpenRig upgrade, systematic debugging, queue triage, or implementation planning; also use when you don't know what applies or nothing is projected on cold boot.
availableCommands.name: $openrig-skills

availableCommands.description: Debug LLM applications using the Phoenix CLI. Fetch traces, analyze errors, structure trace review with open coding and axial coding, inspect datasets, review experiments, query annotation configs, and use the GraphQL API. Use whenever the user is analyzing traces or spans, investigating LLM/agent failures, deciding what to do after instrumenting an app, building failure taxonomies, choosing what evals to write, or asking "what's going wrong", "what kinds of mistakes", or "where do I focus" — even without naming a technique.
availableCommands.name: $phoenix-cli

availableCommands.description: OpenInference semantic conventions and instrumentation for Phoenix AI observability. Use when implementing LLM tracing, creating custom spans, or deploying to production.
availableCommands.name: $phoenix-tracing

availableCommands.description: Run a pre-merge readiness review that combines standard code-review methods with selector-vs-enforcer checks, adversarial mutation of gates, identity/ manifest coverage, claim-vs-mechanism audits, and CI/acceptance gates. Use when the user asks for pre-merge review, merge readiness, /pre-merge-review, "is this PR ready to merge", or a final review before merge after addressing reviewer feedback.
availableCommands.name: $pre-merge-review

availableCommands.description: Guidance for creating, updating, and optimizing Agent Skills — modular skill folders (a SKILL.md plus optional scripts/references/assets) that give an agent procedural knowledge for a specific task or domain. Use this whenever someone wants to build a new skill, turn a repeated workflow into a reusable skill, improve or refactor an existing skill, fix a skill that isn't triggering reliably, or write and critique a SKILL.md and its description — even if they don't say the word "skill" explicitly. Prefer updating a closely related existing skill over creating a near-duplicate.
availableCommands.name: $skill-creator

availableCommands.description: Invoke whenever writing, changing, reviewing, or sweeping tests. Authoring gate for new tests plus audit workflow for low-value, implementation-coupled, or duplicative tests and the test-only production seams they demand.
availableCommands.name: $test-audit

availableCommands.description: Generate or edit raster images when the task benefits from AI-created bitmap visuals such as photos, illustrations, textures, sprites, mockups, or transparent-background cutouts. Use when Codex should create a brand-new image, transform an existing image, or derive visual variants from references, and the output should be a bitmap asset rather than repo-native code or vector. Do not use when the task is better handled by editing existing SVG/vector/code-native assets, extending an established icon or logo system, or building the visual directly in HTML/CSS/canvas.
availableCommands.name: $imagegen

availableCommands.description: Codex models/pricing, scheduled tasks, skills, settings, setup, troubleshooting, and self-knowledge; OpenAI APIs and ChatGPT Work. 'You'/'this app' means Codex only.
availableCommands.name: $openai-docs

availableCommands.description: Perform a read-only, defect-first review of a specified code change and return every actionable finding. Use when another agent delegates review of uncommitted changes, a base-branch diff, a commit, or custom review instructions.
availableCommands.name: $review-agent

availableCommands.description: Install curated skills from openai/skills or other repos
availableCommands.name: $skill-installer
